# Shun Yanagisawa (柳沢 俊)

> Market infrastructure practitioner and author, based in Tokyo. His work asks one question — how do humans design trust and order within complex, uncertain systems — through two books (a professional treatise on derivatives clearing and an SF novel), bilingual (English/Japanese) essays, and Clearing Notes, ongoing writing that continues where the clearing book ends. A specialist in derivatives central clearing (OTC clearing, CCP architecture, FX prime brokerage, and Japan rates market infrastructure). Full career history and roles are on the CV page.

## Main pages

- [Home / Profile](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/): The site's central question — how humans design trust and order within complex, uncertain systems — with the author's two books, bilingual essays, and Clearing Notes.
- [Book — デリバティブ・クリアリングのすべて](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/book): Japan's first full-length professional treatise on derivatives clearing (2026).
- Book — Derivatives Clearing: A Comprehensive Guide (Risk Management, Regulation, and the Future of the Markets): the English edition of the same work, ISBN 978-4-9914987-0-1, first edition August 2026 (forthcoming; an English preview of the Introduction and Chapter 1 is on SSRN).
- [Full CV](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/cv): Career history, publications, and credentials in full.
- [Speaking history](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/speaking): Panels, moderated sessions, and speaking engagements.
- [Media appearances](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/media): Press coverage and media mentions.
- [All essays index](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/essays/): The full, newest-first list of bilingual essays.

## Clearing — derivatives clearing, written by the author of the standard Japanese text (bilingual shell, Japanese-language body)

Short pieces placed on the chapter structure of "デリバティブ・クリアリングのすべて" (Shun Yanagisawa), recording what moved in clearing regulation after the first edition. Each piece is written from primary sources and carries its first-publication date. The index, each piece's title/lead, and the glossary shell carry an English/Japanese toggle; the body of each piece is Japanese-language prose, with a 4-6 paragraph English-language summary placed right after the lead so an English reader always has the conclusion and key sources even where the body itself is not translated.

- [クリアリング — 章立て / Clearing index](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/): Bilingual shell (English/Japanese toggle) over the chapter structure below.
- [クリアリング用語集 / Clearing glossary](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/terms): A standalone glossary of derivatives clearing — Japanese-language definitions (CCP, default waterfall, initial and variation margin, cover-n, skin in the game, auto-liquidation), with English abbreviations, formal English names, category filters, official-site source links, and alternative Japanese renderings where translations differ in practice. Seeded from the back matter of "デリバティブ・クリアリングのすべて" and expanded independently as post-publication pieces introduce new terms. The glossary shell (title, intro, category filters, count) has an English/Japanese toggle; the term cards themselves carry both a Japanese and an English definition side by side, always shown regardless of toggle state.
- [What Is a Clearing Broker Actually Financing? Intraday Margin Calls and the Credit of Timing](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/intraday-margin-credit): A clearing broker finances the timing gap between paying the CCP's intraday margin call and collecting from its own customer, drawing on LCH's SwapClear cycles, the US residual interest rule (CFTC Reg 1.22), and JSCC's interest rate swap clearing.
- [Institutionalizing Direct Clearing: What Changes — and What Remains — Once Credit Extension Is Removed](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/direct-clearing-credit-boundary): The CFTC's December 2025 RFC draws the regulatory boundary at whether the customer's maximum loss is prefunded before the position exists, not at asset type — and prefunding still leaves customer asset segregation and settlement finality unresolved.
- [Who Bears the Legal Obligations When Clearing Bypasses the FCM? The Regulatory Gaps Left by Retail Direct Clearing](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/direct-clearing-regulatory-gap): Removing the FCM does not remove the legal obligations — customer identification, AML, disclosure, asset protection — that attach to the direct customer relationship; FIA and ISDA comment letters show where those obligations currently have no home.
- [Can Auto-Liquidation Replace the FCM? The Limits of Leveraged Direct Clearing](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/auto-liquidation-limits): Auto-liquidation can replace an FCM's collateral-triggered intervention but not its credit assessment or liquidity provision, and it assumes an order can execute at the intended price — an assumption that breaks down when prices gap and order books thin, with the 2022 UK LDI crisis read here as a similar margin-call/asset-sale amplification, not an auto-liquidation failure.
- [Is Japan's Retail FX Market a Precedent for Direct Clearing? Where Loss-Cut Operations Converge — and Loss Allocation Diverges](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/japan-otc-margin): Japan's OTC retail FX dealers are a complete bilateral model, not an unfinished CCP — a precedent for customer-level risk management, but not for CCP-style mutualized loss allocation.
- [How Far Can Margin Be Predicted? What International Guidance Asks of Margin Simulators and Transparency](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/clearing/margin-simulator-transparency): The 2026 CPMI-IOSCO consultation sets "replicability" as its goal and proposes margin simulators as one of the means of reaching it, but FIA/ISDA and CCP Global read where transparency's job actually lies very differently.

## Notes

- Central theme: "In complex, uncertain systems, how do humans design order and trust?"
- The English edition of the derivatives clearing book (ISBN 978-4-9914987-0-1, first edition August 2026, forthcoming) has an English-language preview — the Introduction and Chapter 1, 123 pp. — readable at [/book](https://www.shun-yanagisawa.com/book).
